Understanding How Furniture Gets Dirty

Your furniture is made up of the outer layer of upholstery and the inner layers of cushioning, all of which can get dirty. Dirt starts on the very surface of your furniture, then makes its ways through the various layers to get stuck inside.

Anything that sits on the surface of your furniture for an extended period of time will have a chance to get lodged inside the furniture, including liquids and solids. While these contaminants make their way through your furniture, they can do permanent damage to the structure and appearance of the furniture.

Dirt and dust can be abrasive on the upholstery fibers as they make their way into your furniture. They actually tear the fibers of your furniture apart and will make it look fuzzy or frayed in the long run. Liquids dye the fibers and change their appearance, resulting in a stain. This goes the same in your kitchen, so, make sure that you thoroughly clean your kitchen countertopsas well.

Vacuuming Is Key To Maintaining Your Furniture

One of the best tools you can employ to maintain your furniture is a vacuum cleaner. If you don’t have one of these devices, it might be time to invest in one so that your furniture can keep looking its best. Vacuums lift up dirt and debris before it has an opportunity to get stuck in your upholstery.

You should vacuum your furniture on a regular, frequent basis. Once per week is the minimum you should do, and you need to get the vacuum out anytime there is a spill. Having a strong vacuuming routine will keep your furniture looking good.

A cordless vacuum will be a big help motivating you to vacuum more often. Having to pull out a corded vacuum and negotiate getting it over to your furniture is enough to make you put off the task for a week or two. Buying a cordless vacuum will make you take better care of your furniture.

Keep Shoes Off Of The Furniture

One sure fire way to wear out a piece of furniture before it needs to be thrown away is to wear your shoes on it. Shoes carry a lot of dirt and are too hard for the delicate upholstery of your furniture. You need to remove your shoes before putting your feet on your furniture.

Your shoes are designed to protect your feet out on the street. They pick up all sorts of dirt and grime, and they don’t belong on your furniture. This is a pretty simple rule that all too many people break, and then wonder why their furniture is wearing out.

The upholstery on your furniture is meant to have your skin or your clothing on top of it, not shoes. It simply can’t take the hard surface and dirt that your shoes present to it. Clean Up Spills As Soon As Possible

Accidents are destined to happen, no matter how hard we try to protect our furniture. When something does spill onto your furniture, you must act as fast as you can and clean the spill up. This will help to stop dirt, debris and liquids from getting too deep into the upholstery of your furniture.

When it comes to liquids, the best technique for cleaning a spill is to blot at the spill with a clean, dry cloth. Don’t rub against the spill, because that type of action can actually work the liquid deeper into the furniture. Eventually it won’t be able to come out with traditional methods.

For dry spills, clean with your hands if you can, then reach for the vacuum to get the smaller pieces of the spill. This will help you stop the offending pieces from getting worked too far into the furniture to where it could do real damage.

Use Different Cleaner On Different Spills

Stains are the greatest fear many people have for their furniture. Luckily there are normally solutions that can help you prevent stains from happening. Some of the household cleaners that can help prevent and eliminate stains from setting in are:

  • Vinegar – this acidic liquid breaks down many different stains, including coffee, grass, gum, vomit and juice. If you’re not sure how to remove a stain, try vinegar and it might work.
  • Baking Soda – this household item is the best option if you’re worried about smells from your stain. This is a great option for cleaning furniture that has oil on it.
  • Salt – Sprinkle some table salt on an oily stain, let the oil absorb into the salt, then vacuum it all up.
  • Hydrogen Peroxide – This liquid is the best option for blood or rust stains. Just put some hydrogen peroxide on, wait a few minutes, then blot it up.
  • Dish Soap – this kitchen essential can also be useful on many stains in furniture cleaning. It has great grease lifting properties.

Always try your cleaning product on an inconspicuous part of the furniture to ensure that it won’t damage the upholstery. Once you are sure it is ok for cleaning your furniture, you do it as soon as you notice a stain and you might be able to get rid of it.

There are also a myriad of stain removers available at grocery stores that you can try. Get one that matches your stain or your furniture’s upholstery material.
